title: Oops! 10 Double Faults and a Super-Fast Loss—But This Tennis Champ Still Smiled
summary: Imagine practicing for months, dreaming of winning Wimbledon in front of your home crowd—and then everything goes wrong. That's what happened to Great Britain's Alfie Hewett on Sunday. He was playing Japan's Tokito Oda in the men's wheelchair singles final, and his serve just wouldn't cooperate. Hewett hit three double faults in his very first service game. By the end of the first set, he had six. For the whole match? Ten double faults! In tennis, a double fault means you miss both serves and just hand the point to your opponent. It's like giving away free goals in soccer. Oda, the 20-year-old defending champion, took full advantage. He zoomed to a 6-1, 6-1 victory in under an hour. That's a super-fast match, even for wheelchair tennis. Afterward, Hewett was disappointed but still found a way to joke. "I don't think Tokito read the script," he said, meaning the plan was for Hewett to win! He also congratulated Oda, who has now won six Grand Slam singles titles in a row. That means Oda hasn't lost at any of the four biggest tournaments since early 2025. Hewett and Oda have been the two best players for years, winning every Grand Slam since 2023. But right now, Oda is on top. "Hopefully someone can stop him," Hewett said with a grin. For now, the speedy Japanese star is unstoppable.
why_it_matters: Even when you practice hard and dream of winning, things can go wrong on a big day; what matters is staying positive and finding a way to joke about it, like Hewett did.

background_read: Alfie Hewett is one of the top wheelchair tennis players from Great Britain, and Tokito Oda, from Japan, has become the world's best young player.
Wimbledon is the oldest tennis tournament in the world, held each summer in London, and it includes wheelchair events.
Wheelchair tennis allows the ball to bounce twice, and players use special sport wheelchairs.
Article_Structure: WHO: Alfie Hewett (British player) and Tokito Oda (Japanese defending champion)
WHAT: Hewett lost the Wimbledon wheelchair singles final quickly, making 10 double faults, while Oda won easily 6-1, 6-1.
WHY: Hewett's serve did not work well, giving away points, and Oda was very sharp and fast.
